stem.en: Kabir says a termite "must have a stronger stomach than me, because it eats wood". What is the difference?

text.en: The termite keeps microbes in its gut whose cutters fit the beta link. Kabir's cutters fit only alpha. Strength has nothing to do with it; fit does.

feedback.en: Wood in the strongest stomach acid is still wood. The link needs a cutter shaped for it.

text.en: Termites eat a different kind of wood.

feedback.en: Soft or hard, it is cellulose. The link is the same.

text.en: Termites do not really digest it.

feedback.en: It passes through Kabir. A termite gets most of its food from it, through its microbes.

explanation.en: Cellulose is glucose, and glucose is food, if you have the cutter. Cutters are shaped, and shapes are Book IV's next rung.
